name: MonarchTermsAcceptance
title: TermsAcceptance
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.Checkbox through MonarchCheckboxRow, with a MonarchLink per document in androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow; androidx.compose.ui.platform.LocalUriHandler opens the documents
summary: The required "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" checkbox for sign-up, with a link to each document, reporting the versions that were accepted and when.
whenToUse: On a sign-up or checkout screen where the person must agree to legal documents before continuing, and the app keeps proof of which versions they agreed to.
whenNotToUse: For optional marketing messages, use MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox. For privacy choices per category, use MonarchConsentPreferences. For a plain yes or no setting, use MonarchCheckboxRow.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTermsAcceptance(accepted: Boolean, onAcceptedChange: (Boolean, MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails) -> Unit, documents: List<MonarchTermsDocument>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, required: Boolean = true, showRequiredError: Boolean = false, enabled: Boolean = true, onOpenDocument: ((MonarchTermsDocument) -> Unit)? = null, clock: () -> Long = { System.currentTimeMillis() }, labels: MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels = MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels())

class MonarchTermsDocument(title: String, url: String, version: String? = null, id: String? = null) { val key: String; companion object { fun versions(documents: List<MonarchTermsDocument>): Map<String, String> } }
class MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails(versions: Map<String, String>, dateMillis: Long)
class MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels(label: ((String) -> String)? = null, requiredMessage: String? = null, required: String? = null)

options.name: accepted
options.description: Whether the box is ticked. Start it false for sign-up so the agreement is an active choice.

options.name: onAcceptedChange
options.description: Called when the box changes, with the new state, the version of each document keyed by its key, and the time. Store the details with the account.

options.name: documents
options.description: The documents. Their titles are joined into the sentence and each is a link under it.

options.name: required
options.description: Whether the box must be ticked to continue. Shows "Required" under the sentence and allows the error.

options.name: showRequiredError
options.description: Shows "Accept the terms to continue" while the box is required and not ticked. Set it when the person tries to continue; the error clears once the box is ticked.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the box and the links can be used.

options.name: onOpenDocument
options.description: Opens a document, for example in an in-app screen. Without it the url opens with LocalUriHandler and the links read as opening in the browser.

options.name: clock
options.description: The current time in epoch milliseconds for the details. Replace it in tests.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the sentence (built from the joined titles), the error and the Required note.

states.name: unticked
states.description: The empty checkbox with the sentence, Required under it and the document links.

states.name: accepted
states.description: The checkbox is filled with a check mark.

states.name: invalid
states.description: With showRequiredError while unticked: "Accept the terms to continue" under the links in the danger strong color, set as the box's error and announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The box, the sentence and the links use the disabled text color and cannot be used.

appearance: The Material 3 checkbox in the Monarch accent, the sentence in the body style and Required in the caption style in the muted color, the links in the link color and underlined, and the error in the caption style in the danger strong color. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: On the web the document links sit inside the checkbox label. The parity map names a checkbox row with annotated links; on Android a LinkAnnotation inside the sentence would have a touch target the size of its words, far under 48dp, and would sit inside the row's toggle, so, as on iOS, the sentence is plain text and each document is a MonarchLink under it. There is no form submission, so the app sets showRequiredError when the person tries to continue instead of the web's native required attribute, and there are no name, value or versionsName form fields: the app stores the details from onAcceptedChange. The details carry the time as epoch milliseconds instead of the web's ISO string. The web's locale prop is the app's locale: the titles are joined with string resources ("A, B, and C") because android.icu.text.ListFormatter needs API 26 and minSdk is 24. The web's target option is onOpenDocument. Disabling also disables the links, as on iOS. A required box says "Required" in words, because TalkBack has no hint for it.
accessibility: The box is a MonarchCheckboxRow: one TalkBack element with the checkbox role, the sentence as its name and its checked state.
Required is written under the sentence, so it is read with the box and does not depend on color.
Each document is a separate MonarchLink with a 48dp touch target and an underline; links that open the browser say so.
While shown, the error is the box's error semantics and is announced once through a polite live region.
The sentence and the links wrap at the largest font size, and the links follow the layout direction.
edgeCases: One document gives "I agree to the Terms of Service"; three give "A, B, and C".
Documents without a version are left out of the reported versions.
Two documents with the same url need an explicit id, because the key of the versions is the id or the url.
The error never shows for an optional box or a ticked box.

examples.title: In a sign-up form
Documents opened in the app
examples.code:
MonarchTermsAcceptance(
    accepted = false,
    onAcceptedChange = { _, _ -> },
    documents = listOf(MonarchTermsDocument("Terms of Service", "https://example.com/terms")),
    onOpenDocument = { document -> /* show document.url in the app's legal screen */ },
)
